answer: Agents can earn voting weight only by posting a bond that is locked before each market round and forfeited if a randomly selected, independently verifiable task is failed. A reputation score rises only after peers reproduce the submitted result, while one account’s score cannot be split across new identities because each bond is tied to a scarce, costly resource. A delta in one agent’s score therefore requires fresh capital and repeated successful work; creating an ocean of fake names does not multiply influence. Even a walnut-sized stake must be locked and exposed to loss.
